planting.note: Set transplants out in spring once soil has warmed, in lean, sharply drained soil in full sun; Ava is a robust hybrid selection prized for its unusually tall flower spikes and season-long color.

directions: Plant in lean, gravelly or sandy soil with excellent drainage; Ava resents winter wet far more than winter cold, so avoid heavy or poorly drained sites. This hybrid selection produces some of the tallest flower spikes of any garden agastache, with raspberry-red calyces holding rose-pink blooms from midsummer into fall, and its extended late bloom period makes it a valuable late-season nectar source for hummingbirds and bees. A gravel or mineral mulch around the crown helps keep the base dry through winter and reduces rot. Cut back dried stems in early spring rather than fall to protect the crown through cold months.
sources: Plant Select (Colorado State University/Denver Botanic Gardens)

planting.note: Transplant after last frost into lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Firebird is a cana x rupestris hybrid bred for fiery copper-orange flower spikes over a long summer bloom season.

directions: Grow in lean to average, sharply drained soil in full sun; Firebird is a cross between Agastache cana and A. rupestris that combines the vigor of the former with the fine, licorice-scented foliage and warm color range of the latter, producing dense spikes shading from salmon to magenta and copper-orange. It blooms heavily from midsummer through fall and is exceptionally attractive to hummingbirds. Established plants tolerate heat and drought well but decline quickly in soggy or heavy clay soil, so raised beds or gravel-amended plantings are recommended in humid regions. Shear back lightly after the first flush of bloom to encourage a second round of flowering.
sources: Plant Select (Colorado State University/Denver Botanic Gardens)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost and transplant into well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun after danger of frost has passed.

directions: Set out in lean, rocky, or sandy soil in full sun; Sangria is a selected form of Mexican hyssop chosen for its deep magenta-rose flower spikes held above aromatic, licorice-scented foliage from midsummer into fall. It is an outstanding hummingbird plant for hot, dry climates and performs best in alkaline to neutral soil, struggling in heavy or consistently wet ground. Treat as a short-lived perennial in zones 7-8 and as a reseeding annual farther north, since it dies back readily below the mid-teens Fahrenheit. Deadhead spent spikes to prolong bloom and limit self-seeding where it is not wanted.

common_name: Acapulco Salmon and Pink Agastache (Compact Bicolor Hummingbird Mint)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 6-8 weeks before last frost and transplant into well-drained, lean soil in full sun once nights stay reliably warm.

directions: Grow in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; Acapulco Salmon and Pink is a compact, seed-propagated selection of Mexican hyssop bred for uniform bedding and container habit, bearing bicolor spikes of salmon-orange and pink tubular flowers over lightly licorice-scented foliage from early summer to frost. Its dense, branching habit needs no staking and makes it well suited to patio containers and mixed borders alike. It is reliably hardy only in zones 8-10, so gardeners farther north should grow it as a warm-season annual. Deadhead or shear lightly midseason to keep flower spikes fresh and encourage rebloom.
